  Terse gloss: "An interrogative-exclamatory adverb: 'How?' or 'How!' expressing manner or astonishment; rarely 'Where?' in northern dialect."
  Readable gloss: "Built from the interrogative particle 'ay and the demonstrative koh, this adverb asks 'in what manner?' -- slightly more pointed than the simpler eikh. It appears in both genuine questions (Deut 1:12, 'How can I bear your problems alone?'; Deut 7:17) and anguished exclamations (Isa 1:21, 'How the faithful city has become a harlot!'; Lam 1:1, 'How lonely sits the city!'). Lamentations actually takes its Hebrew title from this word. In two occurrences in Song of Solomon 1:7, it functions as 'where?' -- a usage paralleled by Aramaic eikha, suggesting a northern dialectal coloring. Spanish distinguishes the nuances as 'como' (how, manner) versus 'donde' (where)."

    Enriched: An interrogative or exclamatory adverb meaning 'how?' or 'how!' -- asking about manner (Deut 1:12; 7:17; 12:30; 18:21) or expressing astonishment and lament (Isa 1:21; Lam 1:1; 2:1; 4:1-2). The book of Lamentations takes its Hebrew name from this word's opening cry. Spanish 'como' and German 'wie' render both the questioning and exclamatory force, while French 'comment' highlights the manner-focus...
